# korean-word-of-the-day — static word bank and date-pin rotation internals

> [!warning]
> The word bank shape mirrors exactly what the Resting Screen design renders; adding a word is data-only, never a layout change.

## Migrations

N/A: repo owns no database objects.

## DDL surface

N/A: repo owns no database objects.

## Triggers & guarantees

- **Deterministic rotation** — word selection is by local calendar date with no API, tokens, or network involved; the same date always renders the same word.
- **Index 0 pin** — index 0 is `설레다`, so day one matches the approved mockup exactly.
- **Shape completeness** — every word entry carries `ko`, `roman`, `sound`, `pos`, `meaning`, `syl`, and `ex` fields, so the screen can never render blank panels.

## Decision semantics

### Word-of-the-day selection

Inputs: local calendar date, word bank array. Output: the word entry at the deterministic date-derived index.

- The word bank is stored in a global `window.KOREAN_WORDS` array. (words.js:22)
- Rotation is deterministic by date, with no API, tokens, or network involved. (words.js:16)
- Index 0 is `설레다` so day one matches the approved mockup exactly. (words.js:17)

### Hero line sizing

Inputs: syllable count of the word's `ko` field. Output: auto-shrink decision.

- The hero line auto-shrinks past 4 syllables. (words.js:19)
- The design breathes best at 2–3 syllables. (words.js:19)

## Constants that matter

| name | value | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| hero auto-shrink threshold | 4 syllables | hero line auto-shrinks past 4 syllables |
| design breathing range | 2–3 syllables | design breathes best at 2–3 syllables |
| index 0 | `설레다` | day one matches the approved mockup exactly |

## Word bank entries

Each entry in `window.KOREAN_WORDS` has the following fields:

- `ko` — Hangul, the hero glyph line.
- `roman` — Revised Romanization of the whole word, the official Latin form.
- `sound` — how it actually sounds, deliberately NOT the same string as `roman`.
- `pos` — part of speech, shown after 'Means ·'.
- `meaning` — the definition line.
- `syl` — per-syllable `[hangul, roman]` pairs for the 'Syllables' block.
- `ex` — `[korean, english]` example sentences for the 'In use' block.
